ing: peeled and cut in chunks; use yuca or potato if needed
chopped, divided; use culantro if you can find it
st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, oregano and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and [[10 cups]] water and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the yam, corn and the remaining salt and simmer for another 25 minutes until the yam is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Mash a few pieces of yam against the side of the pot to thicken the broth slightly.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] of the cilantro and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve in bowls with white rice on the side and the remaining cilantro on top.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wide heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion, bell pepper and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, annatto and tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes to coat the grains.
Pour in [[3.5 cups]] broth and the remaining salt and bring to a boil.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover tightly, reduce to low and cook for 25 minutes.
Scatter the peas and olives on top, cover and cook for 5 more minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve.

ing: with 1 tsp salt dissolved, for dipping
st: Cut the ends off the plantains, score the peel lengthwise and peel it off.
Slice the plantains into 1-inch thick rounds.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 325°F (160°C).
Fry the rounds for 3 minutes per side until pale golden and slightly soft.
Lift out onto a plate lined with paper towels.
Press each piece flat with the bottom of a glass or a flat plate to about a quarter inch thick.
Quickly dip each flattened piece in the salted water and pat dry.
Raise the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry again for 2 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain, sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt and serve right away.
Put the beef in a pot with the broth, [[4 cups]] water, the bay leaf and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 1 hour 30 minutes until the beef shreds easily.
Remove the beef and let it cool a little. Shred it with two forks. Keep [[1 cup]] of the cooking liquid.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until they break down.
Stir in the shredded beef, [[1 cup]] reserved liquid, the remaining salt and the pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick and saucy.
Serve with white rice and fried plantains.

ing: peeled, woody core removed, cut in chunks
1 tbsp for the filling, rest for frying
st: Put the cassava in a pot, cover with water, add [[1 tsp]] salt and boil for 25 minutes until very soft.
Drain well and mash while hot until smooth, discarding any stringy fibers. Let cool for 10 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and ground beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until the beef reaches 160°F (71°C) and is no longer pink.
Season with cumin, oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Let the filling cool.
With oiled hands, take a golf-ball-size portion of mashed cassava and flatten it in your palm.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center and fold the cassava over it, shaping an oval roll with sealed edges.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the rolls in batches for 4 minutes until deep golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

ing: for frying, plus 2 tbsp for the dough
st: Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[0.75 cup]] warm water until a soft dough forms, adding a splash more water if dry.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into 10 balls and roll each into a circle about quarter inch thick.
Poke each with a fork a few times so they puff evenly.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 360°F (180°C).
Fry each round for 1 to 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with cheese, eggs or syrup.

ing: such as corvina or sea bass, cut in half-inch cubes
such as habanero or aji, seeded and minced
st: Buy the freshest fish from a trusted seller and keep it very cold until you use it.
Place the fish cubes in a glass or ceramic bowl and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Pour [[1 cup]] lime juice over the fish so it is almost covered.
Stir in the red onion, celery and chili.
Cover and refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes until the fish turns opaque and firm.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] cilantro and the pepper.
Taste and add more salt or lime if needed.
Serve cold right away in glasses or bowls with crackers or fried plantain chips.
Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the pigeon peas, rice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and [[1.5 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let it steam, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve alongside fried fish or chicken.

ing: masa harina or precooked corn flour
or foil, to line the dish
st: Put the chicken in a pot with [[6 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt and simmer for 35 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken, shred the meat and save [[5 cups]] of the broth.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion, pepper and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes, then stir in the shredded chicken, remaining salt and pepper to make the filling.
In a large pot, whisk the cornmeal with [[5 cups]] warm broth until smooth.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until it becomes a thick dough-like porridge.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking dish with banana leaves or foil.
Spread half the cornmeal in the dish, top with the chicken filling, olives, raisins and capers, then cover with the rest of the cornmeal.
Fold the leaves over, cover tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

ing: made into fine shaved ice with a blender or ice shaver
or make the syrup below with 1 cup mashed berries
st: Make a quick syrup by heating [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[0.5 cup]] water until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] lime juice and cool completely.
Mix the cooled syrup with your fruit syrup, or use [[0.5 cup]] ready fruit syrup as is.
Shave the ice finely in a blender or shaver and pack it into four cups.
Pour the syrup generously over each cup so it soaks in.
Drizzle [[1 tbsp]] condensed milk over each portion.
Serve immediately with a spoon or straw before it melts.
